history.summary: Split follows time spent and client-driven rework. Jun did the most hours across four cuts and the export, Mina wrote three script versions, and Sora recorded the voiceover three times.

reasons.text: Wrote script v1 and shaped the whole video; 165 minutes total.
Reworked the script after client feedback (shorter intro, product close) and fit it to 28 seconds.
Four edit cuts plus export, 265 minutes, the most time of anyone.
Fixed subtitles to one line and re-synced the new voiceover after client feedback.
Recorded the voiceover and delivered the best take.
Re-recorded the full voiceover twice for a warmer tone, as the client asked.

history.summary: Jun gets the largest share for the most time and four edit cuts plus export. Mina shaped the script and reworked it after feedback. Sora recorded and twice re-recorded the voiceover.

history.changedBecause: No change: Jun's dispute asks for 70% because editing is hard, which is a claim about the role and a demand for a number, not evidence. I checked Jun's work in the log (e07, e09, e11, e13, e14: 265 minutes, four cuts plus export) and the v1 split already counts all of it and gives Jun the largest share. The log shows no extra Jun work that was missed.

disputes.text: Re-recording 3 wasn't logged: after Re-recording 2 (e12) I recorded pickup lines for the closing line, and they went into the final cut (e13).
disputes.answer: Sora's dispute (d2) rests on a line Sora added (e16). It fits the order of events (after e12, before final cut e13) and nothing in the log contradicts it, so the extra 22 minutes count and Sora goes from 16% to 19%. Jun's dispute (d1) only says editing is hard and asks for 70%. That is not evidence, and Jun's edit work (e07, e09, e11, e13, e14) was already counted. Jun gives up 3 points to pay for Sora's increase.

AI (Claude) revised the split to v3. Approvals were reset.
